judged_text: The diff bundles an entire RSS/Atom feed-polling subsystem (hourly scheduled job, three new site settings, simple-rss gem dependency, and a synchronous RSS branch inside TopicRetriever) that is not traceable to the stated embed URL handling and validation intent. Every deployment of this PR gains a permanently scheduled hourly job that fetches and parses an external URL and creates/updates topics, even for sites that only wanted iframe embedding; the feature cannot be evaluated or reverted independently of the embed-comment feature it rides in with.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does bundle a substantial feed-import feature set alongside iframe embedding: new gems (`simple-rss`, `ruby-readability`), new scheduled job `Jobs::PollFeed` with `recurrence { hourly }`, new site settings under `embedding:` (`feed_polling_enabled`, `feed_polling_url`, `embed_by_username`), and a synchronous branch in `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` that runs the poller when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true. However, the finding overstates impact: the hourly job’s `execute` method only calls `poll_feed` when `feed_polling_enabled?` and required settings are present, so it does not “fetch and parse an external URL” on every deployment by default. The core concern (feature coupling/PR scope and inability to evaluate/revert independently) is still real and grounded in the diff, but it’s not a directly verifiable bug.
